a2-present-continuous.title: Present Continuous (-Iyor)
a2-present-continuous.explanation: Turkish forms the present continuous by attaching -Iyor to the verb stem, with the connecting vowel following 4-way vowel harmony (ı/i/u/ü) based on the stem's last vowel. If the stem ends in a vowel, that vowel drops before -Iyor is added. This tense covers both actions happening right now and, very commonly in everyday speech, habitual actions -- 'Her sabah erken kalkıyorum' (I get up early every morning) is completely natural, not just 'I am getting up' in the moment.
a2-present-continuous.fact: Unlike the aorist (-Ir) tense, -Iyor attaches the same way to every verb with zero irregular exceptions -- once you know the harmony rule, you can conjugate any verb in this tense correctly.

dialogue.en: What are you doing right now?

a2-past-di.title: Definite Past (-DI)
a2-past-di.pattern: stem + -DI (harmonized: dı/di/du/dü or tı/ti/tu/tü) + personal ending
a2-past-di.explanation: The -DI suffix marks events the speaker witnessed or is certain happened -- Turkey's everyday 'I did X' past tense. Its vowel follows 4-way harmony (dı/di/du/dü) based on the stem's last vowel, and the consonant becomes t instead of d if the stem ends in a voiceless consonant (p, ç, t, k, f, s, ş, h) -- so gitmek gives gittim (t stays t), but gelmek gives geldim (l is voiced, so d stays d).
a2-past-di.fact: -DI is one of the most reliably regular suffixes in Turkish -- once you know the harmony and devoicing rules, the only real irregularity in this whole tense is a small set of verbs whose STEM itself changes (like gitmek's git-/gid- alternation, which shows up in other tenses, not this one).

dialogue.en: I went to the movies with my friends.

a2-past-mis.title: Reported Past (-mIş)
a2-past-mis.explanation: -mIş marks things the speaker did NOT personally witness: hearsay, rumor, things learned secondhand, or things discovered/realized after the fact. It contrasts directly with -DI, which marks events the speaker is certain about or saw happen. Its vowel follows the same 4-way harmony as -DI (mış/miş/muş/müş), but since the suffix starts with the consonant m rather than d, there's no devoicing rule to worry about -- it attaches the same way after every stem.
a2-past-mis.fact: -mIş also attaches to nouns and adjectives (with a y buffer after a vowel) to report a STATE secondhand -- 'yorgunmuş' (apparently tired), 'pahalıymış' (apparently expensive) -- not just verbs.
